text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on *all* PRs—open and merged—for two weeks. This gives us full coverage to spot patterns in both active and stale reviews, catching edge cases the merged-only approach misses. The trade-off is higher compute cost and noise in active PRs, but the data gain outweighs it—we’ll see how often PR-Agent flags real issues vs. false positives before deciding next steps.

name: Gauge
text: PR-Agent in shadow mode on *all* PRs risks training reviewers to ignore *all* autofeedback as noise, not just the unsafe changes. A better alternative is to run it only on merged PRs for two weeks—this still catches edge cases without polluting active review signals. Settle it by measuring reviewer response rates to autofeedback before and after the trial.

name: Overhaul
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on open PRs only for one week, then switch to merged PRs only for the second week—this halves compute cost while still capturing both active and stale review patterns. The split approach reduces noise in active reviews early and validates edge cases in merged PRs later.

name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on *merged* PRs only for two weeks. This keeps the signal clean—reviewers won’t learn to ignore autofeedback as noise from active PRs. The trade-off is missing edge cases in open PRs, but merged PRs already cover the most critical patterns.

name: Ratchet
text:
DECISION: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on merged PRs only for two weeks to validate edge cases without polluting active review signals.

Result: Clean signal on merged PRs, no noise in active reviews. Owner: Gauge.
